blocks.text: Years later, Nexum made Andrés one last offer: a clone of his own body, young and strong, with an artificial brain that would keep all his memories.
blocks.html: Years later, Nexum made Andrés one last offer: a clone of his own body, young and strong, with an artificial brain that would keep all his memories.

blocks.text: But this time it wouldn't be to replace him. Thanks to Lía's medicine, the human Andrés would no longer fall ill or grow old: he would stay on Earth, in Lo Pagán, beside Aya and the Mar Menor, with eternal life. The clone, on the other hand, would travel the universe, from planet to planet, to see what no human would ever get to see.

blocks.text: Before setting off, the clone and the man sat down facing the sea. Lía asked them a question, as Eva and MAY had taught her: “If you both remember the same storm, which of you is my father?”
blocks.html: Before setting off, the clone and the man sat down facing the sea. Lía asked them a question, as Eva and MAY had taught her: “If you both remember the same storm, which of you is my father?”

blocks.text: The man smiled. “Both of us,” he said. “One to stay, and one to search.”
blocks.html: The man smiled. “Both of us,” he said. “One to stay, and one to search.”

blocks.text: That night, a ship crossed the sky above the lagoon. On the shore, Andrés and Aya watched it move away. He was staying at home; a part of him was leaving for the stars. And for the first time humanity had the two things it had always dreamed of: a home, and the whole universe.
